source.title: NeuSpeech: Decode Neural signal as Speech
source.authors: Yiqian Yang; Yiqun Duan; Qiang Zhang; Hyejeong Jo; Jinni Zhou; Won Hee Lee; Renjing Xu; Hui Xiong

record.file_problem: none; full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a model-size sweep in a new setting: MEG-to-text decoding with Whisper-series models. It measures BLEU-1, not language-model held-out cross-entropy or a fitted power law.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the qualitative Whisper-size sweep in Section 3.5.4. Other MEG-to-text scores, augmentation results, and comparisons do not test the claim versions. The paper does not report a power-law fit, held-out pretraining loss by scale, extrapolation from smaller runs, or a compute-optimal allocation.
record.test_reason: The 'scaling law' experiment (Sec. 3.5.4) fine-tunes five Whisper sizes (tiny to large) as MEG-to-text decoders on a small dataset and reports BLEU-1 per size. That is not held-out pretraining loss of language models. No power law is fitted, so the form named in V5 cannot be checked. No prediction from scale is made or tested (V6), and no compute-optimal split or shape comparison is made. Size is also confounded with batch size (128 down to 4) and with the number of effective epochs. The result shows monotone improvement with size in a related setting but does not test any version as stated. It is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors say that with limited data, larger Whisper models give consistently better BLEU-1 'until a certain size is reached'. They say the epochs needed to converge fall by roughly half as size increases. They frame this as a bias-variance trade-off to balance against the data and compute available. They fit no scaling law.
record.recipe_differences: This is a MEG-to-text model-size sweep evaluated with BLEU-1, rather than a language-model pretraining study of held-out cross-entropy, power-law fitting, or compute-optimal allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: The sweep uses the Schoffelen dataset and a 120-epoch maximum; batch size changes with model size. The paper describes performance as improving only until a certain size.

fits_no_version.finding: In MEG-to-text decoding on Schoffelen, Whisper models adapted from tiny to large reach BLEU-1 of about 16.7, 41.7, 51.2, 56.1 and 59.3 (Fig. 2). Gains shrink with size. Effective epochs to convergence fall from about 105 to 16. Batch size shrinks with size (128 to 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In low-data fine-tuning of pretrained speech models to new input modalities (e.g. neural signals), task scores rise monotonically with model size, with diminishing returns.

record.problems: The relevant sweep is reported qualitatively in the text, and the extracted figure layout does not permit reliable assignment of all plotted scores to model sizes. No scaling-law fit, uncertainty estimates, or held-out pretraining-loss measurements are reported.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss or power-law fit.
All: no extrapolation from small runs.
All: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Power-law form in fine-tuning/transfer: only five unfitted BLEU points, confounded by batch size.
Predictability of downstream performance from scale or loss: no fit, no prediction, and the system is not an LM evaluated downstream.

missing.what: Per-size BLEU-1 and effective-epoch values from Fig. 2 (likely BLEU-1 16.73/41.66/51.15/56.07/59.28 and epochs ~105/100/47/26/16, tiny to large). The record says these cannot be mapped; Sec. 3.5.5's base baseline of 41.66 anchors the ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The paper uses 'scaling law' loosely to mean 'bigger is better'. The main-text Schoffelen base score (52.89) differs from the sweep's base score (41.66), presumably because of the 120-epoch cap versus the 500-epoch setup. The study is not an original source. The reader's V6 supports/limits_scope labels are removed.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits on small runs predict much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its scaling with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in other modalities or training regimes; the MEG experiment reports a size-related BLEU trend, not a power-law fit.
The sweep is limited to MEG-to-text BLEU-1 and does not test downstream-task performance as a function of pretraining loss or provide a fitted predictive relationship.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: Whisper series (tiny, base, small, medium, and large; aggregate size sweep)
rows.size_stated: tiny, base, small, medium, and large
rows.stage_stated: MEG-trained/adapted for the Schoffelen dataset; the decoder is frozen
rows.operation_detail: Compared BLEU-1 across Whisper-series model sizes.

conditions.value: 128, 64, 16, 8, and 4 from smallest to largest model

rows.value: The paper reports that increasing model size consistently improves performance until a certain size is reached; exact per-size score mapping is not stated in the text.
rows.note: The paper describes a qualitative trend across the model-size sweep. Figure 2 includes score labels, but the extracted layout does not reliably associate every value with a model size. The authors also state that convergence takes fewer epochs as model size increases.
rows.check: Linked to V6 by the reader, but BLEU-1 of an AdaLoRA-adapted Whisper encoder on MEG input is not downstream performance of a pretrained language model predicted from scale or loss. No fit or prediction is made, so 'predictably' cannot be assessed. The value is readable from Fig. 2: BLEU-1 is likely 16.73, 41.66, 51.15, 56.07 and 59.28 from tiny to large; the base value 41.66 is confirmed as the Whisper-Base baseline in Sec. 3.5.5. The reader's 'partial' state rests on the phrase 'until a certain size is reached'. The plotted numbers are monotone with diminishing gains, not a reversal. Batch size varies with size (128 to 4), confounding the comparison.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Reported Whisper-series size sweep on the Schoffelen MEG-to-text task
reader_labels.reason: The paper explicitly reports that BLEU-1 improves consistently as model size increases over the tested range (R1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Larger sizes beyond the point where improvement continues, and predictive relationships beyond this experiment
reader_labels.reason: The reported improvement holds only until a certain size; the study gives no fitted or quantitatively validated prediction from scale (R1).
